solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aid for businessman likely to go in cut

indicators.note: to go in tells us one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
apt means likely, as in apt to happen

explanation.surface: A tool for an executive that is likely to be axed in a round of cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable computer is the travelling executive's standard working tool.

clue.text: According to their horoscope their life is in the balance

definitions.text: According to their horoscope their life is in the balance

parts.words: According to their horoscope their life is in the balance
parts.note: people born under Libra, whose zodiac sign is the scales or balance

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the balance' sounds like a life at risk; here it means born under the sign of the scales.
explanation.definitionFit: People born under the zodiac sign of the scales take their name from that sign.

clue.text: Used for getting in the drink — after opening time?

definitions.text: Used for getting in the drink — after opening time?

parts.words: Used for getting in the drink — after opening time?
parts.note: a pilot may land in the sea using one, once it has opened

explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting in the drink after opening time' suggests buying a pint once the pub opens; it is landing in the sea after the canopy opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy device that opens to slow a fall, and may drop someone into the sea.

clue.text: Refuse of autumn left out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out tells us a letter is dropped from the season's name

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Someone declines the autumn season, with the left wing excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: rubbish, waste parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the waste parts of a butchered animal, so it counts as refuse.

clue.text: Yet it's not the place for a deep sleep

definitions.text: Yet it's not the place for a deep sleep

parts.words: Yet it's not the place for a deep sleep
parts.note: a bed that lies very deep, under the sea

explanation.walkthrough: A 'bed' suggests sleep, and this one is very deep, but nobody sleeps on the sea floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor of the sea is a bed in the geographical sense, lying very deep.

clue.text: Firm provided headgear

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A company that supplied hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A coif is a close-fitting cap, an item of headgear.

clue.text: One element that may be split into many

indicators.note: split means the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemical element that can be divided into a great number of parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a metalloid chemical element, symbol Sb.

clue.text: Novel house, but starting to let rain in

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a roof that leaks lets rain in

explanation.surface: A new house, but one whose roof is beginning to let in water.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Dickens's novel Bleak House: this word plus 'house' names the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novel Bleak House supplies the word placed before 'house' in its title.

clue.text: Make converse?

parts.note: converse is used as an adjective meaning opposite: the opposite of making

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make converse' looks like 'get someone talking'; converse means opposite, and the opposite of making is wrecking.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck is the reverse of to create or build, the converse of making.

clue.text: Deprived — due to faulty beer measure!

indicators.note: faulty means the letters are wrongly arranged

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for feet, a measure

explanation.surface: Someone is left without because a measure of beer was poured badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means deprived of something, left without it.

clue.text: I'm set back by the strain of being a teacher

indicators.note: set back means the two letters are turned round

parts.note: I'm gives the letters I and M
stress means strain

explanation.surface: Someone feels set back by the pressure of working as a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a female teacher, often shortened to the bare title.

clue.text: Put on finery and rode out

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dressed up in fine clothes and went riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To be decorated or dressed up means to have put on finery.

clue.text: Royalty's own touch of honour

parts.note: the tap on the shoulder with a sword given by the monarch when knighting someone

explanation.walkthrough: The 'touch' is literal: the sovereign touches the shoulder with a sword when conferring a knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial tap of a sword marking a knighthood, now any award or praise.

clue.text: The object of his match is a draw

definitions.text: The object of his match is a draw

parts.words: The object of his match is a draw
parts.note: he strikes a match to light his pipe and take a puff, a draw

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' and 'draw' suggest a game ending level; here a match is lit so a pipe can be drawn on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who uses tobacco lights a match in order to draw on a pipe or cigarette.

clue.text: Give authority to mounted soldiers to secure prisoner

indicators.note: to secure means to hold something inside
in a down clue, mounted means the word is read upwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Cavalry are authorised to guard a captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted soldiers' looks like cavalry, but 'mounted' turns REME upwards to EMER, which holds POW.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them authority to act.

clue.text: Live ammunition?

parts.note: a bullet is a ..., and so is a living garden creature

explanation.walkthrough: 'Live ammunition' usually means real bullets; here it is a bullet word that is also a living creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is both a bullet and a slimy living mollusc, so it is ammunition that lives.

clue.text: Head ball on to right winger

parts.note: a prom is a dance, a ball
taken as written
a Tory is a Conservative, someone on the political right

explanation.surface: A footballer heads the ball across to the winger on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: 'Head' is a headland and 'right winger' a political Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a headland, a high point of land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Away from business, look gloomy and out of sorts

parts.note: off means away from
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
to lour is to frown or look sullen

explanation.surface: Someone off work looks miserable and feels unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly unwell or not oneself is being out of sorts.

clue.text: Company with deficit states huge figure

parts.note: a loss is a deficit
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A firm with a shortfall reports a very large number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Huge figure' suggests a big number on the balance sheet; it is a giant statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a gigantic statue, like that of Rhodes.

clue.text: Men on phone exchange will be a rarity

indicators.note: exchange means the letters swap places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Men chatting on the telephone exchange would be unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' here is the anagram signal, not a telephone exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon can be a remarkable or exceptional thing, something rare.

clue.text: Loyal toasts drunk in hock, presumably

definitions.meaning: toasts drunk to the monarch, vows of loyalty
items left in pawn as security for a loan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' and 'hock' (a German wine) suggest drinking; 'in hock' means pawned.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasts are pledged to someone's health, and goods pawned are held as security, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Sheriff yet to catch suspect

indicators.note: to catch means the letters are held within the words

explanation.surface: The sheriff has still to arrest the suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for dubious or suspect.

clue.text: Where a suspended sentence was carried out for old sailors

definitions.text: Where a suspended sentence was carried out for old sailors

parts.words: Where a suspended sentence was carried out for old sailors
parts.note: condemned sailors were hanged from the end of a spar on the ship

explanation.walkthrough: A 'suspended sentence' is normally a lenient penalty; here it means a sentence of hanging, carried out from the spar.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of a ship's spar was used for hanging offenders at sea.

clue.text: This has been used poetically in the past

definitions.text: This has been used poetically in the past

parts.words: This has been used poetically in the past
parts.note: a poetic, archaic phrase meaning before this time

explanation.walkthrough: The clue works twice: the phrase means 'in the past' and it is also an old poetic usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic, poetic expression meaning before this time, previously.

clue.text: Run out of pictures to put up

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of

indicators.note: in a down clue, to put up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: art means pictures

explanation.surface: Someone has no pictures left to hang.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run not scored off the bat, like a wide, is an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a run added for a wide or no-ball is called an extra.

clue.text: Beat this for a political slogan

definitions.meaning: split as two words, an exhortation to be a supporter of the British Labour Party

explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a major British political party; split in two the word becomes a campaign call.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone soundly, or to go on about a point far too long, is to keep beating it.

clue.text: A Roman nose initially put off the scent

indicators.note: put off means a letter is removed
initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Roman's nose first lost the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell or scent.

clue.text: New vote for prohibition

indicators.note: new means the letters are formed afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh ballot to ban something.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a ban or prohibition on something.

clue.text: Get blooming old?

parts.note: plants past flowering produce seed; people grow shabby with age

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British oath, 'get bloody old'; it means flowering plants going past their best.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for running down or becoming shabby comes from plants that stop flowering and produce seed.

clue.text: Capital of Tobago? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly names the capital of Tobago.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia.

clue.text: A picture of vessels returning gunfire

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels
a shot is gunfire

explanation.surface: A painting of ships firing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships under fire; they are pans.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick photograph, a picture.

clue.text: Something the barber may rub around?

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A barber massaging something into a customer's scalp.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one picture of the barber at work, but 'around' is the anagram signal acting on 'may rub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay rum is a fragrant hair lotion that barbers traditionally apply to customers.
